title: Charcoal and kaolin face mask
subtitle: A rinse-off clay mask for oily and combination skin
excerpt: A dry clay mask powder of kaolin, activated charcoal, and sea salt that is mixed fresh with water or rose water before each use. Draws surface oil and grime from the pores. Makes enough powder for 15 masks.
sourceNotes: Kaolin clay in cosmetic masks: CIR Expert Panel safety assessment (2012, open access). Activated charcoal in skincare: general cosmetic science reference on adsorption and surface-active ingredients. Sea salt as mineral addition in cosmetic preparations: general reference.

recipe.yieldDescription: ~75 g dry powder (enough for 15 masks at 5 g per use)
recipe.batchNotes: Make 150 g at a time for more uses. The dry powder is stable for a year.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make the dry blend in advance and mix fresh with liquid before each use.
recipe.shelfLifeNotes: The dry powder keeps one year in a sealed jar in a dry cupboard. Mix only as much as needed for one use with water or rose water; the mixed paste does not keep. Discard the dry powder if it clumps, smells off, or absorbs moisture.

glossaryTerms.definition: A fine white clay mineral (aluminium silicate) used in cosmetic masks and powders. It is the mildest of the cosmetic clays, suitable for most skin types including sensitive. It draws surface impurities and excess oil into the clay matrix as the mask dries.

content.text: This is a dry powder mask that you mix fresh with a little water or rose water before each use.

forms the base; activated charcoal darkens the mask and adds some surface-adsorption action; fine sea salt provides a mild mineral. The mask suits oily and combination skin. Limit use to once a week on normal skin; twice weekly on oily skin.
Do not use on broken, sunburned, or strongly reactive skin. Patch test on the jaw before the first full-face application.

items.prepNote: cosmetic-grade fine kaolin clay; 67% of dry blend
food- or cosmetic-grade activated charcoal powder; 27% of dry blend
fine sea salt; 7% of dry blend; mineral addition

content.text: Combine the kaolin clay, activated charcoal, and sea salt in a bowl. Stir well until the charcoal is evenly distributed through the clay (the mix should be a uniform dark grey). Spoon into a sealed glass jar.
Measure 5 g (about 1 level teaspoon) of dry powder into a small bowl or the palm of your hand.
Add enough water or rose water to form a paste: typically 8 to 10 ml. The paste should be smooth and spreadable, not runny.
Apply to the face in a thin layer, avoiding the eye area and lips. Leave for eight to ten minutes. Do not allow the mask to dry completely and crack; rinse when it is still slightly tacky.
Rinse thoroughly with warm water and pat dry. Follow with a moisturiser.
The dry powder keeps one year in a sealed jar. Always use a dry spoon to measure. Do not store the mixed paste; use it immediately.
